# A throwing afterSetMounted makes the next update re-insert its siblings

## Context

Found while fixing realworld2 on 2026-10-20 (#19891, #19892). Its home view rendered twice, with 23 duplicate element ids and one uncaught `TypeError` reading `subscribe`. The trigger was app-level: `PreviewList`, a `list.Base`, calls `Neo.main.addon.Navigator.subscribe()` in `afterSetMounted` (`src/list/Base.mjs:343`), and realworld2's addon list had dropped `Navigator`. #19892 restored the addon. The engine defect it exposed is still on `dev`: one component whose `afterSetMounted` throws corrupts the vdom state of its parent's subtree.

Observed: the doubled view, the 23 duplicate ids and the TypeError (realworld2 before #19892). Inferred from source, below: the mechanism. AC-1 and AC-2's red arms are its isolated reproduction.

## The Problem

`VdomLifecycle#syncVnodeTree` hands an adopted vnode to every child component in one loop (`src/mixin/VdomLifecycle.mjs:1196-1211`). Setting `component.mounted = true` runs the child's `afterSetMounted` inside that loop. When it throws:
- the loop stops, so every later sibling keeps its previous vnode or none, and stays unmounted;
- the unmount pass (`:1219-1223`) and the receiver's own `_vnode` and `afterVnodeSync` (`:1226-1228`) never run;
- the error leaves `syncVnodeTree` and reaches `executeVdomUpdate`'s catch (`:502`), which treats it as a failed flight. It skips the remaining roots and rejects every root's callbacks, although the main thread has already applied the deltas.

The parent's next update then diffs against a vnode tree without the nodes the DOM already holds, and inserts them again.

## The Architectural Reality

- `syncVnodeTree` (`:1155`) runs for each adopted root from `executeVdomUpdate` (`:476`), and from `afterSetVnode` (`:134`).
- `mounted` is a reactive config. Components wire main-thread addons and DOM listeners in `afterSetMounted` (`src/list/Base.mjs:330-346`), so subclass and app code runs inside the loop.
- The same file already isolates callbacks that may throw, each with a try/catch and `console.error`: `initVnode callback rejection failed` (`:849`), `initVnode deferred update failed` (`:856`), `vdom callback rejection failed` (`:1107`).
- Design authority: the catch's own comment, "Rejection releases every root without acknowledging a vnode it did not receive." A hook that throws after the vnode arrived and its deltas were applied is not that case.

## The Fix

In `syncVnodeTree`'s second pass, wrap each child's mount (`component.mounted = true` and `component.afterVnodeSync(deltas)`) in a try/catch that logs `console.error('syncVnodeTree: a mount hook failed', component.id, error)` and continues. The sync then completes: later siblings get their vnodes, the unmount pass runs, the receiver adopts its vnode, and the flight resolves.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: A unit arm: a child whose `afterSetMounted` throws during its parent's update leaves its later siblings synced (vnode set, `mounted: true`) and the parent's vnode adopted. Red on `dev`.
- [ ] AC-2: A browser e2e (vdom behavior changes need one, per #19499): the parent's update promise resolves, and its next update inserts no node twice, so the page has no duplicate ids. Red on `dev`.
- [ ] AC-3: The thrown error still reaches the console and names the component.

## Out of Scope

- The render paths that mount the rendered component itself (`:821`, `:1016`); a throw there concerns only that component.
- App code that throws in `afterSetMounted`; #19892 fixed realworld2's.

## Avoided Traps

- Re-throwing after the loop: `executeVdomUpdate`'s catch would still reject a flight whose deltas are applied.
- Catching around `syncVnodeTree` in `executeVdomUpdate`: the throwing child's later siblings would still stay unsynced.

syncVnodeTree mounts every child the adopted vnode carries in one loop. A child
whose afterSetMounted threw stopped that loop: its later siblings kept no vnode,
the unmount pass and the receiver's adoption never ran, and executeVdomUpdate
rejected a flight whose deltas the DOM had already applied. The next update
then diffed against references to children without a vnode and inserted them
a second time.

is logged with the component id and the sync completes.
